To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the establishment of a national NCD registry in a small island developing state is feasible and cost-effective, and that such a registry is a valuable tool for monitoring the NCD epidemic, for informing public health policy, and for providing a basis for health care resource planning.

(1) a national registry for chronic NCDs in a small island nation is a feasible and cost-effective approach to collecting data on incident cases of stroke, heart attack and cancer; (2) the registry is a valuable tool for public health professionals to identify and target high-priority health issues; (3) the registry is also a useful source of data on NCDs in small island nations; and (4) the registry is an important source of data for research.
